Streets, schools and getting around Harbour Chines

items.t: Harbour Chines is the "Chines" slope of central Coquitlam served by Como Lake Avenue, adjoining the Chineside sub-area; its boundaries are not verified — no City neighbourhood plan boundary for Harbour Chines is stated on a City page in the sources read, and an official City of Coquitlam neighbourhood plan name for Harbour Chines is also not verified. Nearby areas: Chineside to the west/south-west, Central Coquitlam to the east, Ranch Park to the south, and the City Centre / Pinetree Way edge to the north-east.

Current listing evidence for the sub-area is detached houses only — a current listing page for the area describes tree-lined streets of detached homes, with most homes on lots of 10,000 square feet or more.

Main roads: Como Lake Avenue serves the Chines area; exact sub-area boundary roads are not verified. Como Lake Park is a City park name in City records for central Coquitlam; parks inside Harbour Chines by official name are not verified. The nearest hospital is Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, on the Port Moody / Coquitlam border. The nearest library branch is the Coquitlam Public Library City Centre branch, 1169 Pinetree Way.

blocks.text: Good to know about Harbour Chines

items.t: Filing a Harbour Chines deal in the wrong city changes the taxes, the bylaws and the school district on paper.
The 33% headline ratio rests on three sales.

The density story here is suites and coach homes, not strata. The SSMUH framework (up to 3 units on lots ≤280 m², up to 4 units under 4,050 m²) is the only multi-unit mechanism operating on Harbour Chines streets, and area listing copy markets the large lots for laneway/coach potential — a sub-area can be densifying and still have zero condos.
No Harbour Chines school catchment is verified yet.

Streets, schools and getting around Harbour Chines

items.t: Harbour Chines is a central Coquitlam pocket on the slope above Como Lake Avenue — "chines" being the ravine/valley terrain, and there is no harbour or waterfront in the sub-area despite the name. Its precise boundary roads: Not verified (no City neighbourhood-plan text for "Harbour Chines" has been located; the name functions as a board/statistical sub-area, not a confirmed City plan area).

Do not merge Chineside: Harbour Chines and Chineside are two separate Coquitlam sub-areas with separate rows in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report. Stats, stock and catchments from one never carry to the other.

Medians are community-level only: Coquitlam "Condos & Townhomes" COMBINED median was $625,000 in September 2026 ($687/sqft, 96% sale-to-list, 23 days on market), and the Coquitlam detached median was $1,455,000 — cited exactly as the report states them, never as Harbour Chines figures.

Transit: no station is inside Harbour Chines; the nearest SkyTrain stations are Coquitlam Central and Burquitlam on the Evergreen Extension (Millennium Line); per-route bus numbers for the sub-area: Not verified.

School names that appear on listing pages for Harbour Chines houses (including Harbour View Elementary and Dr. Charles Best Secondary) are listing copy, not district-verified catchments — run the exact address in the SD43 School Locator.

Parks: Como Lake Park is a City of Coquitlam park name for the central-Coquitlam Como Lake area; whether any part of it sits inside this sub-area: Not verified — do not market it as in-area without a boundary source.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Harbour Chines

items.t: City zoning and plan — standing corrections applied (Coquitlam): Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996 — small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3, subdivision minimums 650 m² / 18.5 m width (R-1, R-3) and 465 m² / 12.5 m (R-2). The Interim Official Community Plan — Bylaws 5511/5512, 2026 — was adopted April 27, 2026 and supersedes OCP No. 3479; cite the interim OCP, never 3479.

Presales (REDMA), if any are ever marketed here: a presale buyer must receive the developer's disclosure statement (REDMA s. 18) and has a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing or acknowledging it (REDMA s. 21), with deposits in trust. No presale is verified in Harbour Chines.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Harbour Chines
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established house lots: detached houses on the Como Lake slope under the small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3 in Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996, as the research states them. Lot character, only: subdivision minimums are 650 m² with 18.5 m width in R-1 and R-3, and 465 m² with 12.5 m width in R-2. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot; the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are not verified until checked parcel by parcel. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Coquitlam utility charges cover water, sewer and drainage and solid waste; lots not connected to municipal water or sewer are outside the SSMUH rules, so property-level septic or well status is not verified — confirm servicing for the specific parcel with the City.
ALR vs non-ALR: parcel-level ALR status for Harbour Chines: Not verified in the sources read; no ALR percentage split is stated. Check any parcel in the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder.

Watercourse position: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam; Zoning Bylaw s.519 sets flood protection setbacks and s.523 covers riparian areas. Lot-level status: Not verified per lot.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Harbour Chines

items.t: Bare-land strata block (for the form — no Harbour Chines bare-land strata plan is verified): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Harbour Chines ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31).

blocks.text: Harbour Chines: streets and boundaries

items.t: Harbour Chines is in the City of Coquitlam, not Port Coquitlam, despite the word Harbour.
The area is the Chines slope of central Coquitlam served by Como Lake Avenue, adjoining the separate Chineside sub-area.
Neighbours are Chineside next door, Central Coquitlam to the east, Ranch Park to the south and the City Centre / Pinetree Way edge to the north-east.
Harbour Chines and Chineside are two separate board sub-areas and must not be merged.

blocks.text: Harbour Chines: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The rule that matters most on creek and ravine lots here is the watercourse permit area.

blocks.text: Harbour Chines: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The name is the trap: there is no harbour or waterfront in Harbour Chines.
School District 43 Programs of Choice — French Immersion, Mandarin Bilingual and Montessori — are entered by application, not by catchment.
Cross-catchment applications in SD43 are decided by a lottery / random draw with in-district priority.
The nearest library branch is Coquitlam Public Library City Centre at 1169 Pinetree Way, with the Poirier branch at 575 Poirier Street.
The nearest Evergreen Extension (Millennium Line) stations are Coquitlam Central and Burquitlam; no station is inside Harbour Chines.

blocks.text: Harbour Chines: costs and taxes

items.t: The Harbour Chines-specific point is the municipality itself: taxes are Coquitlam taxes, due July 2, 2026, not Port Coquitlam taxes.
Coquitlam is listed as a taxable area for the provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax, so every residential owner must complete the annual declaration.
